# A 100.00 USD invoice settled by the customer's whole 100.00 USD credit, which
# the block gives by guid so this tool carves it rather than GnuCash. Nothing is
# left of the credit, so there is no remainder.
#
# The credit came in under a CAD transaction, so what it cost is readable from
# that transaction rather than from a stored key — which is what makes the split
# a cost basis again if the record it settles here is ever unposted.
#
# `auto_apply_credit: true` must not be used here. On 3.8, 4.4 and 4.13 the
# engine's own application rewrites the credit split's value at par — −100.00
# where −137.00 belongs — and adds a balancing 37.00 USD split to cover the
# difference, so the book under test would be a different book on those builds.
# See CLAUDE.md finding 19.
invoice "INV-FX-SPENDS-CREDIT"
	customer_id: "C-FX"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-03-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-03-01
		description: "More consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-03-01
		due: 2026-04-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-FX-SPENDS-CREDIT"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		amount: 100.00
		from_credit: true
		credit_dated: 2026-02-25
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		txn_split_guid: "SPLIT_GUID"
